plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following conditions is NOT mandatory for a registered person to avail Input Tax Credit (ITC) under Section 16(2) of the CGST Act, 2017?
options: Possession of a tax invoice or debit note issued by a registered supplier
Receipt of goods or services or both
Filing of the annual return by the recipient for the relevant financial year
Furnishing of the return under Section 39 by the registered person
plain.explanation: Section 16(2) prescribes four primary conditions for claiming ITC: possession of tax invoice/debit note, receipt of goods/services, tax charged has been paid to the government, and furnishing of the return under Section 39. Filing of the annual return is not a pre-condition for availing ITC during the financial year.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: M/s. ABC Ltd. purchased machinery worth Rs. 10,00,000 (exclusive of GST at 18%) for factory use. The company capitalized the full invoice value including the GST component of Rs. 1,80,000 in its books of accounts and claimed depreciation on the total capitalized amount under the Income-tax Act, 1961. What is the correct position regarding ITC on this machinery?
options: ITC can be claimed fully along with depreciation on the GST component
ITC cannot be claimed on the GST component since depreciation has been claimed on it under the Income-tax Act
ITC can be claimed up to 50% of the GST amount and depreciation on the remaining 50%
ITC can be claimed by reversing the depreciation subsequently within 30 days
plain.explanation: As per the proviso to Section 16(3) of the CGST Act, 2017, if the registered person has claimed depreciation on the tax component of the cost of capital goods and plant and machinery under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the input tax on the said component shall not be allowed as ITC.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the time limit for availing Input Tax Credit under Section 16(4) of the CGST Act, 2017 for any invoice or debit note relating to a financial year?
options: Due date of filing return for the month of September of the subsequent financial year
Actual date of filing of the annual return for the relevant financial year or 30th November of the subsequent financial year, whichever is earlier
31st December of the subsequent financial year
Actual date of filing of the annual return for the relevant financial year or 30th November of the subsequent financial year, whichever is later
plain.explanation: Section 16(4) mandates that ITC pertaining to any invoice or debit note can be availed up to the earlier of: (i) the thirtieth day of November following the end of financial year to which such invoice/debit note relates, or (ii) the date of furnishing of the relevant annual return.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: An invoice was issued by a supplier on 15th October 2024 for FY 2024-25. Due to an oversight, the recipient did not claim the ITC in time. What is the maximum date up to which the recipient can avail ITC on this invoice, assuming the annual return for FY 2024-25 is filed on 31st December 2025?
options: 30th November 2025
31st December 2025
15th October 2025
30th September 2025
plain.explanation: As per Section 16(4), the time limit is the earlier of 30th November of the subsequent financial year (30th November 2025) or the date of filing the annual return (31st December 2025). Thus, 30th November 2025 is the correct date.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: When goods are received in lots or installments by a registered person, when can the Input Tax Credit be claimed against the tax invoice?
options: When the first installment of goods is received
When the last lot or installment of the goods is received
Proportionately as and when each lot or installment is received
Only after the invoice is fully paid within 180 days
plain.explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), where the goods against an invoice are received in lots or installments, the registered person shall be entitled to take input tax credit upon the receipt of the last lot or installment.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If a recipient fails to pay to the supplier the value of goods or services along with the tax payable thereon within what period from the date of issue of invoice, an amount equal to the ITC availed is required to be added to output tax liability along with interest?
options: 90 days
180 days
270 days
365 days
plain.explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), if the recipient fails to pay the value of supply plus tax within 180 days from the date of issue of invoice, an amount equal to the ITC availed shall be added to their output tax liability, along with applicable interest.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following inward supplies is NOT blocked under Section 17(5) of the CGST Act, 2017?
options: Motor vehicles for transportation of persons having approved seating capacity of not more than 13 persons (including driver), used for general business travel
Food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, except where outward taxable supply is of the same category
Goods or services used for personal consumption
Motor vehicles used for transportation of goods
plain.explanation: Under Section 17(5), motor vehicles for transportation of goods are explicitly excluded from the blocked credit category, meaning ITC is available on them. The other three options represent blocked credits under Section 17(5).

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 17(5), ITC is available on motor vehicles having a seating capacity of not more than 13 persons (including driver) when they are used for which of the following specified purposes?
options: Transportation of employees to and from workplace as a statutory obligation
Further supply of such vehicles, or transportation of passengers, or imparting training on driving such vehicles
General conveyance of the Managing Director for business meetings
Leasing or renting of vehicles for employee recreation trips
plain.explanation: Section 17(5)(a) blocks ITC on motor vehicles for transportation of persons <= 13 capacity, except when they are used for making taxable supplies of: (i) further supply of such vehicles; (ii) transportation of passengers; or (iii) imparting training on driving such vehicles.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 deals with the reversal of Input Tax Credit in respect of inputs and input services used for which type of supplies?
options: Exclusively taxable supplies
Exclusively exempt supplies
Both effected for business purposes and non-business/personal purposes, or partly for taxable and partly for exempt supplies
Capital goods used for both taxable and exempt supplies
plain.explanation: Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the manner of determination of eligible input tax credit in respect of inputs or input services and reversal thereof when used partly for business/non-business or partly for taxable/exempt supplies. Rule 43 deals with capital goods.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the useful life in quarters considered for calculation of reversal of ITC on capital goods used commonly for taxable and exempt supplies under Rule 43 of the CGST Rules, 2017?
options: 20 quarters (5 years)
60 quarters (15 years)
10 quarters (2.5 years)
36 quarters (9 years)
plain.explanation: Under Rule 43 of the CGST Rules, 2017, the useful life of any capital goods is taken as 5 years from the date of invoice, which equates to 20 quarters. The common ITC attributable to exempt supplies is calculated on a quarterly pro-rata basis over this period.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: When a registered person switches from the regular scheme to the Composition Scheme under Section 10, how must they treat the ITC lying in their electronic credit ledger on the day immediately preceding the date of switch?
options: They can carry forward and utilize the credit against future composition tax liability

They must pay an amount equivalent to the credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock, and capital goods, by debiting electronic credit or cash ledger
The credit automatically lapses and cannot be adjusted
They can claim a full cash refund of the balance from the department
plain.explanation: As per Section 18(4) read with Rule 44, a registered person opting for composition levy must pay an amount equal to the ITC in respect of inputs in stock, semi-finished/finished goods in stock, and capital goods, computed as prescribed, which results in reversal/payment.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Mr. X, an unregistered person, gets registered voluntarily under Section 25(3) on 15th August. What is his entitlement regarding ITC on inputs held in stock on the day immediately preceding the date of grant of registration?
options: He is eligible to claim ITC on inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day preceding registration
He is eligible to claim ITC on all capital goods and inputs held in stock for the past 2 years
He is not eligible for any ITC on prior stock since registration is voluntary
He can claim ITC only if the stock was purchased within 30 days prior to registration
plain.explanation: Under Section 18(1)(a), a person who applies for registration within 30 days of becoming liable to register, or voluntarily under Section 25(3), is entitled to take credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day immediately preceding the date of grant of registration.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the time limit for issuing the declaration in Form GST ITC-01 by a person who has become liable to register and seeks to claim ITC on inputs held in stock under Section 18(1)?
options: Within 30 days from the date of becoming liable to register
Within 30 days from the date of grant of registration
Within 90 days from the date of filing the registration application
Within the due date of filing the annual return
plain.explanation: Rule 40(1)(a) requires any person who takes ITC under Section 18(1)(a) or (b) to make a declaration in FORM GST ITC-01 within 30 days from the date of becoming registered (i.e., grant of registration).

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If a registered person transfers their business consequent to change in ownership (like amalgamation or merger), how is the unutilized ITC in the electronic credit ledger transferred to the new entity?
options: It lapses completely and cannot be transferred
It is transferred using Form GST ITC-02, provided the scheme of merger/amalgamation has specific provisions for transfer of liabilities
It can be transferred only with the written permission of the jurisdictional Commissioner
It is transferred via Form GST ITC-01
plain.explanation: As per Section 18(3) read with Rule 41, in case of amalgamation, merger, demerger, or change in ownership, the unutilized ITC can be transferred to the transferee entity using Form GST ITC-02, provided the restructuring specifics include liabilities.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following is treated as 'exempt supply' for the purpose of reversal of ITC under Rule 42 and Rule 43?
options: Supply of goods or services or both which attracts zero rate of tax
Supply of goods or services or both which are chargeable to nil rate of tax and non-taxable supplies, including transactions of private securities or sale of land/building (where specified)
Only supplies made to SEZ units
Export of goods under bond without payment of IGST
plain.explanation: Explanation to Chapter V (Rules 42 and 43) clarifies that 'exempt supply' includes supply of any goods or services or both which attracts nil rate of tax or which may be wholly exempt from tax, and includes non-taxable supply. However, export of goods/services and supplies to SEZ are not treated as exempt supplies for this reversal.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a registered person claim Input Tax Credit on goods or services used for constructing an immovable property (other than plant and machinery) on their own account, even if such property is used in the course or furtherance of business?
options: Yes, full ITC is available since it is used for business
No, ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(c) and (d) except in the case of plant and machinery
Yes, ITC is available up to 50%
No, ITC is blocked unless capitalization is avoided
plain.explanation: Under Section 17(5)(c) and (d), ITC is blocked on works contract services and goods/services received by a taxable person for construction of an immovable property on their own account, other than plant and machinery, even if used in the course or furtherance of business.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What happens to the ITC availed on inputs that are subsequently written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples?
options: It can be retained without any reversal
It must be reversed under Section 17(5)(h)
It must be claimed as an additional business expense under Income-tax Act
It is treated as outward taxable supply and tax is paid at market value
plain.explanation: Section 17(5)(h) explicitly blocks ITC in respect of goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples. Therefore, any ITC availed on such goods must be reversed.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: According to Rule 36(4) of the CGST Rules, 2017, Input Tax Credit to be availed by a registered person in respect of invoices/debit notes not reported by suppliers in their GSTR-1/IFF can be availed up to what limit?
options: Up to 5% of the eligible credit available in respect of reported invoices
Up to 10% of the eligible credit available
Zero percent (ITC can be availed only to the extent details are communicated in GSTR-2B/GSTR-1)
Up to 20% of the eligible credit available
plain.explanation: Rule 36(4) was amended to state that no ITC can be availed by a registered person in respect of invoices/debit notes unless the details of such invoices/debit notes have been furnished by the supplier in GSTR-1/IFF and communicated to the recipient in GSTR-2B. The earlier 20% and 5% conditional buffers are no longer applicable.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following persons is eligible to claim ITC under GST?
options: A person paying tax under the Composition Levy under Section 10
A non-resident taxable person for all inward supplies
A registered person making taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies
A person exclusively engaged in supplying goods/services that are wholly exempt from tax
plain.explanation: Only registered persons making taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) are eligible to claim ITC under Section 16(1). Composition dealers, exempt suppliers, and non-resident taxable persons (except on imported goods) cannot claim regular ITC.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: When capital goods on which ITC has been availed are subsequently sold or supplied by a registered person, how is the tax payable on such disposal calculated?
options: GST is payable on the full transaction value
GST is payable on the higher of: (a) tax on the transaction value, or (b) tax on the ITC availed on such capital goods reduced by prescribed percentage points per quarter, whichever is higher
GST is exempted on second-hand capital goods
GST is payable only on the book value as per balance sheet
plain.explanation: As per the proviso to Rule 40(2) / Section 18(6), where capital goods on which ITC has been taken are supplied, the registered person shall pay an amount equal to the ITC taken reduced by 5 percentage points per quarter from the date of invoice, or the tax on transaction value, whichever is higher.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can a principal claim ITC on inputs sent directly to a job worker's premises without the goods first coming to the principal's business premises?
options: No, goods must first be received at the principal's factory before being sent to a job worker
Yes, provided the principal receives the goods back within 1 year for inputs and 3 years for capital goods
Yes, the principal can take ITC upon receipt of goods by the job worker, provided other conditions are met
No, ITC is blocked when goods are delivered to third party locations
plain.explanation: As per the first proviso to Section 16(2)(b), for the purpose of claiming ITC, goods delivered by the supplier to a recipient's job worker on the direction of the registered person shall be deemed to have been received by the registered person.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the maximum time period within which inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back to the principal's place of business to avoid being treated as a deemed supply?
options: 1 year from the date of receipt by the job worker
3 years from the date of receipt by the job worker
180 days from the date of dispatch
6 months from the end of the financial year
plain.explanation: Under Section 143 of the CGST Act, inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back within 1 year of being sent (or received by the job worker) failing which it shall be deemed to have been supplied by the principal to the job worker on the day the inputs were sent.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: What is the time limit for bringing back capital goods (other than moulds and dies, jigs and fixtures, and tools) sent to a job worker, to avoid deemed supply treatment under Section 143?
options: 1 year
2 years
3 years
5 years
plain.explanation: Under Section 143(1)(b), capital goods sent to a job worker must be returned to the principal's place of business within 3 years of being sent, otherwise it is treated as a supply from the date of original dispatch.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: In cases where a tax demand is confirmed against a taxpayer involving fraud, willful misstatement, or suppression of facts, can the taxpayer pay such tax demand utilizing the balance available in their electronic credit ledger?
options: Yes, electronic credit ledger can be used for any tax demand under the Act
No, Section 49(3) / Rule 86B restrict the use of electronic credit ledger for payment of self-assessed tax only, and Section 49(10) restricts payment of demands arising out of fraud
Yes, up to 50% of the demand can be paid from the credit ledger
No, tax demands can only be paid via cash ledger, but interest and penalty can be paid from credit ledger
plain.explanation: As per Rule 86(2) and Section 49, the electronic credit ledger cannot be used for payment of any tax demand that has been raised under Section 74 (fraud, willful misstatement, suppression of facts). Such amounts must be paid through the electronic cash ledger.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following expenditure incurred by an employer towards employees is NOT blocked for ITC under Section 17(5)?
options: Club membership, health and fitness centre membership
Travel benefits extended to employees on vacation such as Leave Travel Concession (LTC) or home travel concession
Food and beverages / outdoor catering when supplied under a statutory obligation imposed by any law for the time being in force
Life insurance and health insurance taken for employees voluntarily
plain.explanation: Section 17(5)(b)(i) blocks ITC on food, beverages, and outdoor catering, but contains an explicit exception: where the government notifies services which are obligatory for an employer to provide to its employees under any law for the time being in force, ITC is allowed.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: When a registered person dies, and their legal representative continues the business, can the unutilized ITC lying in the electronic credit ledger of the deceased person be transferred to the legal representative?
options: No, ITC lapses upon the death of a proprietor
Yes, via Form GST ITC-02, unutilized ITC can be transferred to the legal representative in case of death of sole proprietor
Yes, automatically without filing any specific form
No, only cash balance can be transferred, not credit balance
plain.explanation: Under Section 18(3) read with Rule 41, in case of death of a sole proprietor, transfer of business to a legal heir allows the transfer of unutilized ITC using Form GST ITC-02, provided the transferee is registered.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: If an outward supply made by a registered person is treated as an exempt supply due to a retroactive notification, and the person has already claimed ITC on inputs used for such supply, what is the consequence?
options: The ITC already claimed remains fully valid and untouched
The person is required to reverse the ITC attributable to such exempt supply as per prescribed rules
The person must surrender their registration certificate
The person can claim a refund of the tax paid earlier
plain.explanation: If a supply becomes exempt subsequently or retrospectively, any ITC claimed earlier on inputs/input services used exclusively or commonly for such supply must be reversed in accordance with the relevant provisions (Rule 42/43).

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Can Input Tax Credit be claimed on goods purchased for personal use or consumption of the proprietor or directors, even if paid through the business bank account?
options: Yes, because business bank account was used
No, Section 17(5)(g) blocks ITC on goods or services used for personal consumption
Yes, provided it is shown as staff welfare in financial statements
No, unless fringe benefit tax is paid
plain.explanation: Section 17(5)(g) specifically blocks ITC in respect of goods or services used for personal consumption. Any purchase for personal use of proprietor, partners, or directors is ineligible for ITC.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Under Section 18(2), no ITC can be claimed by a person in respect of any stock of inputs after the expiry of how many months from the date of issue of invoice relating to such inputs?
options: 12 months
18 months
24 months
36 months
plain.explanation: As per the proviso to Section 18(2), no ITC under sub-sections (1) (a) and (1) (b) shall be granted in respect of inputs held in stock or inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock after the expiry of 1 year (12 months) from the date of issue of invoice relating to such inputs.

plain.subject: Taxation
plain.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the restriction on the use of the electronic credit ledger under Rule 86B?
options: Rule 86B restricts a registered person from using the electronic credit ledger to discharge more than 99% of their output tax liability in cases where taxable supplies exceed Rs. 50 lakhs in a month, subject to specified exceptions.
Rule 86B completely prohibits the use of electronic credit ledger for all taxpayers with turnover above Rs. 5 crores.
Rule 86B restricts ITC utilization for exempt supplies only.
Rule 86B is applicable to all taxpayers irrespective of their tax liability.
plain.explanation: Rule 86B of the CGST Rules, 2017 restricts the use of the electronic credit ledger for discharging output tax liability to 99% in cases where the monthly taxable supply exceeds Rs. 50 lakhs, leaving at least 1% to be paid in cash, subject to certain exceptions like income tax paid in previous years.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s. Zenith Enterprises, a registered GST taxpayer in Maharashtra, purchased a machine for Rs. 20,00,000 plus GST @ 18% on 10th July 2024 for use in its manufacturing unit. The machine was received in two lots: first lot on 1st August 2024 and second lot on 10th August 2024. Zenith Enterprises capitalized the machine in its books including the GST component and claimed depreciation under the Income-tax Act, 1961. The supplier filed GSTR-1 reflecting the invoice on time, and Zenith filed its annual return for FY 2024-25 on 30th September 2025.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the correct date on which Zenith Enterprises is entitled to avail Input Tax Credit on the machinery, assuming all conditions are met otherwise?
options: 1st August 2024
10th August 2024
10th July 2024
30th September 2025
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), when goods are received in lots or installments, ITC can be availed only upon the receipt of the last lot or installment. Since the second lot was received on 10th August 2024, ITC entitlement arises on that date.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can Zenith Enterprises claim ITC on the GST component of Rs. 3,60,000 paid on the machinery?
options: Yes, full ITC can be claimed alongside depreciation
No, because depreciation has been claimed on the GST component under the Income-tax Act
Yes, 50% ITC and 50% depreciation can be claimed simultaneously
No, because machinery is blocked under Section 17(5)
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the proviso to Section 16(3), if a registered person claims depreciation on the tax component of the cost of capital goods under the Income-tax Act, 1961, the input tax credit on such tax component is not allowed.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What would have been the last date for availing ITC on this machinery under Section 16(4), had they not claimed depreciation?
options: 30th November 2025
31st December 2025
30th September 2025
31st March 2025
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 16(4), the time limit for availing ITC for FY 2024-25 is the earlier of 30th November 2025 or the date of filing the annual return (30th September 2025). Wait, since 30th September 2025 is earlier than 30th November 2025, let's check: the annual return was filed on 30th September 2025. Therefore, the earlier of 30th November 2025 and 30th September 2025 is 30th September 2025.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Zenith Enterprises had used this machinery exclusively for manufacturing goods that are wholly exempt from GST, would they have been eligible for ITC?
options: Yes, full ITC is available on machinery used for exempt supplies
No, ITC is not available on inputs or capital goods used exclusively for making exempt supplies
Yes, up to 50% ITC is allowed
No, but a cash refund of the tax paid can be claimed
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 17(2), where the goods or services are used by the registered person partly for effecting taxable supplies and partly for exempt supplies, the ITC is restricted to the quantum attributable to taxable supplies. If used exclusively for exempt supplies, no ITC is available.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: Mr. Sharma commenced a trading business in Delhi and obtained registration under GST on 1st October 2024. Prior to obtaining registration, he had purchased inputs in stock worth Rs. 5,00,000 (exclusive of GST @ 12%) on 15th August 2024. He also purchased a car for business use on 10th September 2024 for Rs. 10,00,000 plus GST @ 28% (seating capacity 5 persons) and capitalized it. On 1st December 2024, he sent inputs worth Rs. 2,00,000 to a job worker for processing.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Mr. Sharma eligible to claim ITC on the inputs held in stock on 30th September 2024 (the day preceding registration)?
options: No, because he was unregistered at the time of purchase
Yes, under Section 18(1)(a) for inputs held in stock on the day preceding registration, provided invoices are within 1 year
Yes, for all purchases made in the last 3 years
No, unless he pays a special composition fee
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 18(1)(a), a person who registers within 30 days of becoming liable is entitled to ITC on inputs held in stock on the day preceding registration, provided the invoice date is not older than 1 year.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the correct treatment of GST paid on the car purchased on 10th September 2024 for business use (seating capacity 5 persons)?
options: Full ITC can be claimed since it is used for business
ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(a) as it is a motor vehicle for transportation of persons <= 13 capacity and not used for specified exceptions
ITC can be claimed up to 50%
ITC can be claimed if depreciation is foregone
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 17(5)(a), ITC is blocked on motor vehicles for transportation of persons with seating capacity <= 13 persons, unless used for specified exempt purposes like further supply, passenger transport, or driving school. General business travel does not qualify.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the maximum time limit within which the inputs sent to the job worker on 1st December 2024 must be brought back to Mr. Sharma's premises to avoid deemed supply?
options: 6 months
1 year
3 years
180 days
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 143(1)(a), inputs sent to a job worker must be brought back within 1 year of being sent, failing which the transaction is deemed to be a supply from the date of dispatch.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which form is required to be filed by Mr. Sharma to claim ITC on inputs held in stock prior to registration?
options: FORM GST ITC-01
FORM GST ITC-02
FORM GST ITC-03
FORM GST REG-01
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 40(1)(a) requires a registered person claiming ITC under Section 18(1) on inputs in stock to file a declaration in FORM GST ITC-01 within 30 days of becoming registered.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s. Apex Technologies Ltd., a registered software company in Bengaluru, undertook construction of an office building on its own account during FY 2024-25. It incurred expenses on works contract services of Rs. 50,00,000 (plus GST 18%) and purchased cement and iron bars locally worth Rs. 30,00,000 (plus GST 18%) used in the construction. Simultaneously, Apex Technologies Ltd. purchased computers worth Rs. 20,00,000 (plus GST 18%) for office use. The company also provided outdoor catering for its employees during an annual corporate event, incurring Rs. 5,00,000 plus GST 18%.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Apex Technologies Ltd. eligible to claim ITC on works contract services used for the construction of its office building?
options: Yes, because the office building is used for business
No, ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(c) on works contract services for construction of immovable property, other than plant and machinery
Yes, up to 50%
No, unless capitalization is avoided
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 17(5)(c), ITC is blocked in respect of works contract services when supplied for construction of immovable property, other than plant and machinery, even if used for business.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the eligibility of ITC on cement and iron bars purchased for the construction of the office building?
options: Full ITC is available
ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(d) for goods received for construction of immovable property on own account
ITC is available subject to 180 days payment condition
ITC is available since they are inputs
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 17(5)(d) blocks ITC on goods or services received by a taxable person for construction of an immovable property on their own account (including building), other than plant and machinery.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can Apex Technologies Ltd. claim ITC on the computers purchased for office use?
options: No, computers are treated as capital goods and ineligible for ITC
Yes, computers are not blocked under Section 17(5) and qualify as capital goods/inputs used in business
Yes, but only if depreciation is not claimed
No, electronics are blocked
linkedMcqs.explanation: Computers used in business are eligible capital goods/inputs for ITC. They are not covered under any blocked credit category in Section 17(5), provided depreciation is not claimed on the tax component.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the tax treatment of GST paid on outdoor catering services for the corporate event?
options: ITC can be claimed fully
ITC is blocked under Section 17(5)(b)(ii) unless outward supply is of the same category or provided under statutory obligation
ITC can be claimed up to 50%
ITC is allowed as staff welfare expense
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 17(5)(b)(ii) blocks ITC on outdoor catering, food, and beverages, except where an outward taxable supply of the same category is made or where it is obligatory for an employer to provide under any law.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s. Beta Industries operates a factory making both taxable goods and exempt goods. During the month of October 2024, it received common inputs worth Rs. 10,00,000 on which total GST paid was Rs. 1,80,000. Total turnover of Beta Industries for the month was Rs. 50,00,000, out of which taxable supplies amounted to Rs. 30,00,000, exempt supplies amounted to Rs. 15,00,000, and zero-rated supplies (exports) amounted to Rs. 5,00,000. Additionally, Beta Industries had availed ITC of Rs. 25,000 on inputs that were destroyed by fire during the month.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which rule governs the reversal of common Input Tax Credit on inputs and input services used for both taxable and exempt supplies?
options: Rule 36
Rule 42
Rule 43
Rule 44
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 42 of the CGST Rules, 2017 prescribes the formula and procedure for determination of common ITC attributable to exempt supplies and its subsequent reversal.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the treatment of ITC amounting to Rs. 25,000 on inputs destroyed by fire?
options: It can be retained in full
It must be reversed under Section 17(5)(h) since goods were destroyed
It can be carried forward as loss
It is adjusted against export benefits
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 17(5)(h), ITC in respect of goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off or disposed of by way of gift or free samples is blocked and must be reversed.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: In computing the proportion of exempt supplies for Rule 42, how are zero-rated supplies (exports) treated?
options: Treated as exempt supplies
Treated as taxable supplies (not included in exempt turnover for reversal computation)
Ignored entirely from total turnover
Treated separately as non-business supplies
linkedMcqs.explanation: For the purpose of Rule 42, zero-rated supplies (exports and supplies to SEZ) are treated as taxable supplies and are not counted as exempt supplies while calculating the reversal ratio.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Beta Industries fails to pay the supplier for the common inputs within 180 days from the invoice date, what action is required?
options: Nothing, since goods were received
An amount equal to ITC availed plus applicable interest must be added to output tax liability
Registration is liable to cancellation
Supplier must refund the tax
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per the second proviso to Section 16(2), if payment is not made within 180 days, an amount equal to ITC availed must be added to output tax liability along with interest.

scenarios.subject: Taxation
scenarios.passage: M/s. Delta Logistics, a registered transport operator, was previously registered under the regular GST scheme. On 1st November 2024, Delta Logistics opted to switch to the Composition Scheme under Section 10. On 31st October 2024, the electronic credit ledger of Delta Logistics showed a balance of Rs. 1,50,000. On the same date, they held inputs in stock valued at Rs. 10,00,000 (GST paid @ 18%, total Rs. 1,80,000) and capital goods on which ITC of Rs. 3,00,000 had been claimed earlier (purchased 1 year ago).

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What are the statutory obligations of Delta Logistics regarding the unutilized ITC and ITC on stock upon opting for the Composition Scheme?
options: They can continue to carry forward the credit balance
They must pay an amount equivalent to the ITC in respect of inputs in stock and capital goods by debiting electronic credit or cash ledger, and remaining credit lapses
They can claim a cash refund of Rs. 1,50,000
The credit ledger balance is transferred to the Government revenue without any calculation
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Section 18(4) read with Rule 44, when shifting to the composition scheme, the registered person must pay an amount equivalent to the ITC on inputs in stock and capital goods (reduced by percentage points), and the remaining balance in the electronic credit ledger lapses.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: How is the ITC reversal on capital goods calculated when shifting to the composition scheme under Rule 44?
options: Full ITC originally claimed must be paid back
ITC is calculated on the remaining useful life in months/quarters on a pro-rata basis
No reversal is required for capital goods
50% of the original ITC is reversed flat
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Rule 44(6), for capital goods held in stock, the ITC taken is computed on the basis of remaining useful life in quarters (taking useful life as 5 years / 20 quarters), and the proportionate amount is added to liability.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the time limit for filing the stock declaration in FORM GST ITC-03 when opting for the composition scheme?
options: Within 30 days from the date of switch
Within 60 days from the commencement of the relevant financial year or within 30 days of opting for composition
Within 180 days
Along with the annual return
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 44(4) mandates that the details of stock and capital goods for payment/reversal under Section 18(4) must be furnished in FORM GST ITC-03 within 60 days of the commencement of the relevant financial year or within 30 days of opting for composition levy.

linkedMcqs.subject: Taxation
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can a composition taxpayer under Section 10 issue a tax invoice to their customers to pass on Input Tax Credit?
options: Yes, exactly like a regular taxpayer
No, a composition taxpayer cannot collect tax from recipients nor issue a tax invoice; they must issue a bill of supply
Yes, but only for inter-state supplies
No, but they can issue a delivery challan
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per Section 10(4) read with Section 31(2), a composition taxpayer cannot collect any tax from the recipient on supplies made by them and cannot issue a tax invoice; instead, they must issue a Bill of Supply and cannot pass on any ITC.
